prOriginal.nota: Upstream calcom/cal.com now redirects to calcom/cal.diy. Found by head branch feat/sync-app-credentials; headRefOid equals benchmark head 9fde0e9 and the squash 824145b0 has an identical diff. Reverted same day (#11450, 2023-09-19) and re-added by #11453 (2023-09-20) with safeParse/.data handling; re-add otherwise kept the bugs.

oauth-credential-sync-and-app-integratio.reason: Today's handler (apps/web/app/api/webhook/app-credential/route.ts, moved to app dir in #19699) still checks `secretHeader !== CREDENTIAL_SYNC_SECRET`. #13907 only renamed the header/secret constants; no constant-time comparison was ever introduced.

#14588 'Credential Syncing Improvements' replaced appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse with safeParse returning 400 on failure. The decrypt/JSON.parse step is still unguarded for 400 (today wrapped in a try/catch returning 500), but the schema-validation 500 described by the bug is fixed.

Today's route.ts still does prisma.credential.findFirst({userId, appId}) followed by create when nothing is found, with the comment 'Can't use prisma upsert'. The Credential model in schema.prisma has no unique constraint on (userId, appId), only indexes.

The merged code (kept by the 2023-09-20 re-add #11453) set the placeholder unconditionally. #11862 restricted it to credential-sync mode (`&& credentialSyncingEnabled`), so normal refreshes no longer overwrite the real token; that code is unchanged today, and Office365 later moved to OAuthManager.

astra.pergunta: Did #11862 (placeholder only when credential sync is enabled) fix real refresh tokens being overwritten by the literal 'refresh_token'?
astra.resposta: Yes; ordinary refreshes no longer get the placeholder; in sync mode the instance does not use its own refresh token, so the reported failure is not reproduced.

oauth-credential-sync-and-app-integratio.reason: The computed-key schema survived the re-add #11453. #13963 'Moving credential syncing to API' replaced it with z.object({access_token}).passthrough().superRefine(requires a numeric field), so other fields are no longer stripped; this is today's code.

refreshOAuthTokens.ts today still returns the raw fetch Response in sync mode. Google Calendar moved to OAuthManager, but hubspot/lib/CrmService.ts still types the result as HubspotToken and reads expiresIn, and zoho-bigin/lib/CrmService.ts still reads tokenInfo.data.error, so those callers keep the mismatched contract.

#11059 was reverted the same day (#11450) and re-added next day by #11453 'with proper handling of safeParse'. The re-add changed parseRefreshTokenResponse to return refreshTokenResponse.data and Google stores {...parsedKey}; today the function still returns .data.

getClient refreshed unconditionally (try/catch added by #11508, file renamed to CrmService.ts by #14272) until #27264, which added an issued_at + token_lifetime validity check with a 5-minute buffer and only refreshes when the token is not valid. Today's CrmService.ts has that guard.

At the merge prisma was only available through a `declare global var prisma` in packages/prisma/index.ts. #11839 'don't declare prisma as a global object and explicitly import it' added `import { prisma } from "@calcom/prisma"` to salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts; the import is present today.

zoho-bigin/lib/CrmService.ts (renamed from CalendarService.ts in #14272) still does `const credentialId = credential.id` and passes credentialId as the userId argument of refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId), which serializes it as calcomUserId.

#11508 'fix: Salesforce by wrapping the refresh logic in a try/catch' replaced `if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw` with `if (!response.ok)`; today's CrmService.ts still checks response.ok. The stale-token part is tracked as #17.

Until #27264 the Connection was built from credentialKey.access_token/instance_url after persisting the refreshed token. #27264 assigns credentialKey.access_token (and this.accessToken/instanceUrl) from the refresh result before building the Connection; credentialKey.instance_url is still not reassigned (minor residual).

astra.pergunta: Did #27264 fix jsforce.Connection being built with pre-refresh credentialKey tokens?
astra.resposta: Yes; after a successful refresh credentialKey.access_token is reassigned before building the Connection; instance_url not reassigned is a minor residual.

oauth-credential-sync-and-app-integratio.reason: #11530 'fix: credential sync app lookup' changed the select to dirName and indexes appStoreMetadata[app.dirName]; today's route.ts keeps that lookup.
